text:
Noah: Customer hit a reproducible issue in the demo where the chat shows a short truncated completion then a second full completion after a flaky reconnect. Seen on mobile webview and desktop with bad wifi.
Lena: Do we have repro steps? Which streaming path?
QA-Sam: Repro on WKWebView and Chrome mobile emulation. Steps: open demo, send a long prompt, then toggle airplane mode for ~700ms. Repro rate ~65%.
Omar: Which client code? fetch+ReadableStream or EventSource?
Noah: fetch + ReadableStream wrapper in the public sample. We use TextDecoder and split on double-newline boundaries, then JSON.parse each data chunk.
Priya: That parsing strategy can fail on two fronts: partial UTF-8 codepoint splits and replayed fragments after resume. If reconnect causes server to replay from an earlier seq, appending new bytes can merge partial JSON and produce duplicates.
Lena: Do server streams contain seq/resume metadata?
QA-Sam: Yes, we saw comment lines like `: resume_id=aa1b seq=402` before disconnect. The demo ignores comments.
Omar: Node SDK has a resume/seq reconciler; browser demo doesn't. Parity gap.
Noah: Short-term mitigation idea: (1) treat repeated final tokens idempotently for the same resume_id+seq; (2) keep a small seenSeq cache and drop duplicates.
Priya: Medium-term: implement streaming-safe decode (preserve tail bytes, use TextDecoder streaming decode), parse SSE comment metadata on-the-fly, and surface seq/resume metadata in the sample UI so we can troubleshoot.
Lena: Also add an opt-in `sseStrictOrdering` flag. Default false to avoid breaking existing demos. If true, client will throw on any detected gap and let the app decide.
QA-Sam: I can add an automated harness that toggles network and simulates background/foreground timings representative of iOS WKWebView. Will capture raw bytes, decoded text, and parsed seqs for failing runs.
Omar: Implementation notes: when reconnect detected, reset partial-line buffer (to avoid merging pre/post reconnect halves), then rely on server resume token to replay missing seqs. When processing incoming events, ignore events whose seq exists in the seenSeq set. Keep window bounded (e.g., 1024 entries). Emit telemetry `sse_seq_rewind` if server resumes from a seq < lastAppliedSeq.
Noah: UX bandaid: ignore duplicate `[DONE]` tokens for the same seq until full fix ships. Low-risk and reduces visible duplication.
Priya: Tests: unit tests for TextDecoder tail handling, unit tests for seq de-dupe logic, integration test injecting duplicate `[DONE]` and partial JSON boundaries, e2e on BrowserStack for WKWebView.
Lena: Please add a short README snippet in the sample repo explaining seq/resume semantics and how to enable the strict flag. A lot of users copy-paste demo code.
stream-bot: Created RED-1400: "browser-streaming: add seq parsing, tail-safe decode, and dedupe window" and assigned to @Omar.
Noah: I'll prototype a small defensive parser change and the duplicate-[DONE] guard behind a feature flag. Once canary builds are out QA-Sam will validate and attach timelines.
QA-Sam: Will run validation across iOS 13-16 and Android webview. If it still repros, I'll attach console logs, raw bytes, and the seq timeline.
Priya: Thanks team. Fixing this will help parity with Node SDK and reduce onboarding friction for mobile demos. :thumbsup:
